Cover an older capital save with a surviving native control slot on a reserve rider and no owned placement row.
source_inspection_only: The two blocking paths below were traced through production code. Neither sequence appears in the candidate gate.

The city projection selects the owner’s existing pet instance. The attack change carries an explicit order on an already-unconscious target through mounted admission. Equipment interaction and attack resolution on this candidate remain unobserved.

findings.actual: ObserveArrangementOnBar skips retirement for an empty link and passes the still-bound index to ObserveAtBoundary. That replaces A’s recorded identity with null. Suspension then marks slot 9 interrupted, and Revalidate can adopt B as its owner on resume. There is a second route through area replay. If resume detects a direct A-to-B change while B is unresolved, it forgets A’s entry. RestorePersistentSlots can then seed the older transfer row into that empty entry, allowing B to acquire slot 9 when it resolves.
findings.blocking_rationale: A city or interior transition can restore a shortcut that genuine companion removal should retire.
findings.expected: Once the service observes that A was removed or replaced, both the live arrangement and any earlier in-world capture of A’s slot stay retired. Temporary non-resolution of A’s unchanged ID preserves slot 9.
findings.requested_correction: Apply the permanent-loss decision before a boundary observation can replace the known pet identity. Ensure an older in-world transfer row cannot recreate an arrangement retired since capture. Preserve fresh-load seeding and same-pet restoration.
findings.requested_evidence: Keep one pair mounted to exercise area suspension and give a second, dismounted rider slot 9. Test a cleared link at suspension followed by B before resume. Also capture A’s row, change to an unresolved B during suspension, resume and replay the rows, then resolve B. In both cases verify slot 9 stays empty and the next save has no kind-6 row for it. Repeat with A’s unchanged ID and verify one restoration at 9.
findings.title: Area suspension and replay can transfer a retired slot to a replacement companion
findings.trigger: A dismounted rider’s pet changes across an area transition while another mounted pair causes KMC to suspend and restore controls.

findings.actual: The handoff identifies an older capital-save shape with a stale native slot and no KMC slot row for the reserve rider. On cold load that rider has no placement entry and has never been observed in the new world. ClassifyArrangementsForCapture visits candidates and observed departures, CaptureAbsentIntent iterates existing entries, and CaptureAndClearManagedHotbarSlots visits candidates plus observed units. All three miss this rider. An immediate city resave can therefore carry the stale native reference again without recording the recoverable index. Disable cleanup uses the same candidate set.
findings.blocking_rationale: This affects existing saves from the reported city scenario. The surviving slot supplies enough information to recover the player’s choice, and leaving its runtime reference in native serialization also undermines cleanup.
findings.expected: A surviving exact public-control binding on an eligible reserve rider supplies its chosen index. An ordinary resave carries that choice in owned rows and clears the runtime binding from native serialization. Disable/removal clears the binding.
findings.requested_correction: Handle surviving public-control bindings on current-world reserve riders when admitting or saving older data. Recover only an identifiable binding, preserve unrelated slots, and include the recovered rider in the applicable serialization and disable cleanup.
findings.requested_evidence: Start a fresh world with a reserve owner, a supported pet, a native public-control binding at 9, no kind-6/7 rows and no prior observation. Save before opening the rider’s bar or returning them to the party. Verify one kind-6 row at 9, one placement record, and no native KMC slot during serialization. Verify cold return restores 9 once and disable clears the surviving binding.
findings.title: An older capital save can leave a reserve rider’s shortcut outside capture and cleanup
findings.trigger: Load an older capital save whose reserve rider still carries a native Mount / Dismount slot but has no owned toolbar row, then save again or disable the mod before that rider rejoins the party.

prior_finding_assessments.rationale: The exact native-invalidation regression now passes for both fact-reactivation orders, and its same-ID control passes. The permanent-loss issue remains in area-boundary observation and in-world replay, where the previous pet’s chosen index can still reach its replacement.

The exact slot invalidation now updates the owning load scope’s outgoing record. Abandonment restores that record when the original player survives, and world replacement discards it. The gate covers reactivated and inactive facts, one restored binding and archive row at 9, deliberate removal, and successful same-ID world replacement.

summary.delivered_behavior: The candidate preserves many toolbar moves and removals across temporary absence, projects eligible owners’ persistent pets into the capital roster, and admits a mounted player’s explicit attack on an already-unconscious enemy. The two city symptoms share a roster transition but have distinct causes.
remaining_owner_review: After correction, verify the chosen shortcut across real capital and interior visits, forced dismount, and saves inside and outside the city.
Select a reserve owner’s pet through Inventory and Character, verify its identity and equipment, change an item, then reload and repeat.

Use matched longbow shots against standing, consciously prone and unconscious enemies at near and normal distances in RT and TB. Check actual rolls, movement, modifiers and action costs using the handoff’s negative controls.
